bank.name: Islamic Calendar & Special Days
bank.subject: Islamic Studies
bank.description: The Hijri lunar calendar, its months, and the special Islamic days and nights.

questions.prompt: The Islamic (Hijri) calendar is based on?
questions.explanation: The Hijri calendar is a purely lunar calendar of 12 months.

questions.prompt: How many months are there in the Islamic calendar?
questions.explanation: The Islamic year has 12 lunar months.

questions.prompt: Which is the first month of the Islamic calendar?
questions.explanation: Muharram is the first month of the Hijri year.

questions.prompt: Which is the ninth month of the Islamic calendar?
questions.explanation: Ramadan is the ninth month, the month of fasting.

questions.prompt: Which is the last month of the Islamic calendar?
questions.explanation: Dhul-Hijjah, the month of Hajj, is the twelfth and final month.

questions.prompt: The first year of the Islamic calendar corresponds to which year of the Common Era?
questions.explanation: Year 1 AH began with the Hijrah in 622 CE.

questions.prompt: Ashura, the day of fasting, falls on?
questions.explanation: Ashura is the 10th of Muharram.

questions.prompt: The Isra and Mi'raj (Night Journey) is commemorated on?
questions.explanation: The Night Journey is remembered on 27 Rajab.

questions.prompt: The birth of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) is commemorated on?
questions.explanation: Eid Milad-un-Nabi is observed on 12 Rabi-ul-Awwal.

questions.prompt: Shab-e-Barat (the night of freedom from fire) is observed on?
questions.explanation: Shab-e-Barat is the night of the 15th of Shaban.

questions.prompt: Laylat-ul-Qadr is most commonly believed to fall on?
questions.explanation: Many believe Laylat-ul-Qadr falls on the 27th night of Ramadan.

questions.prompt: Eid-ul-Fitr is celebrated in which month?
questions.explanation: Eid-ul-Fitr falls on 1 Shawwal.

questions.prompt: The Prophet (PBUH) was born in which year, known as the Year of the Elephant?
questions.explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) was born in 571 CE, the Year of the Elephant.

questions.prompt: The Islamic months begin with the sighting of the?
questions.explanation: Each Hijri month starts with the sighting of the new crescent moon.

questions.prompt: The month of Dhul-Hijjah is especially sacred because of which event?
questions.explanation: Hajj and Qurbani (sacrifice) take place in Dhul-Hijjah.

questions.prompt: Which month follows Ramadan in the Islamic calendar?
questions.explanation: Shawwal comes directly after Ramadan.

questions.prompt: The Islamic calendar is based on which cycle?
questions.explanation: The Hijri calendar is a pure lunar calendar of 354 or 355 days.

questions.prompt: Which is the second month of the Islamic calendar?
questions.explanation: The order begins: Muharram, Safar, Rabi-ul-Awwal...

questions.prompt: In which month was the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) born?
questions.explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) was born in Rabi-ul-Awwal, in the Year of the Elephant.

questions.prompt: Which month is called the 'month of Allah'?
questions.explanation: Muharram is called 'Shahrullah' (the month of Allah).

questions.prompt: The 27th of Rajab marks which event?
questions.explanation: The 27th of Rajab is observed as the night of the Prophet's (PBUH) journey and ascension.

questions.prompt: The 15th of Sha'ban is known as?
questions.explanation: Shab-e-Barat falls on the 15th night of Sha'ban, observed with prayers and forgiveness.

questions.prompt: Fasting in the month of Shawwal (six days) is considered?
questions.explanation: Fasting six days of Shawwal is recommended; with Ramadan it is like fasting the year.

questions.prompt: Which month follows Dhul-Hijjah?
questions.explanation: Dhul-Hijjah is the 12th month; the new year begins with Muharram.

questions.prompt: The first ten days of which month are considered the best days of the year?
questions.explanation: The first ten days of Dhul-Hijjah are praised in the Quran and hadith as the best days.

questions.prompt: The lunar year is shorter than the solar year by about how many days?
questions.explanation: The Hijri year (354-355 days) is about 10-11 days shorter than the Gregorian year.

questions.prompt: The 1st of Muharram marks what?
questions.explanation: 1 Muharram is the beginning of the Hijri new year.

questions.prompt: Fasting on the 9th and 10th of Muharram is recommended because?
options: It expiates the sins of the previous year
It was the Prophet's habit only
questions.explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) said fasting Ashura expiates the previous year's sins.

questions.prompt: In which month is the Umrah recommended and fasting optional (Sha'ban-style)?
options: Rajab was not singled out; Umrah is valid all year
questions.explanation: Umrah can be performed at any time; scholars caution against singling out Rajab as superior.

questions.prompt: The nights of the last ten days of Ramadan include?
questions.explanation: Laylat-ul-Qadr lies in the last ten odd nights of Ramadan.

questions.prompt: Which month is called the 'month of the Quran'?
questions.explanation: Ramadan is the month in which the Quran was revealed.

questions.prompt: The 10th of Dhul-Hijjah is?
questions.explanation: Eid-ul-Adha falls on 10 Dhul-Hijjah.

questions.prompt: In which month do Muslims observe the fast of Ashura?
questions.explanation: Ashura (10 Muharram) is observed with fasting.

questions.prompt: The forbidden months for fighting (in the pre-Islamic and early Islamic tradition) are?
questions.explanation: The four sacred months are Muharram, Rajab, Dhul-Qa'dah and Dhul-Hijjah.

questions.prompt: Which months are known as the 'Hajj months'?
questions.explanation: The Hajj months are Shawwal, Dhul-Qa'dah and the first ten of Dhul-Hijjah (2:197).

questions.prompt: Which month follows Muharram?
questions.explanation: Safar is the second month.

questions.prompt: The Day of Arafah falls in which month?
questions.explanation: Arafah is on 9 Dhul-Hijjah.

questions.prompt: The Islamic New Year begins with:
questions.explanation: The Hijri year starts on 1 Muharram.

questions.prompt: In which month is the Prophet's (PBUH) birth celebrated as Eid Milad-un-Nabi?
questions.explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) was born in Rabi-ul-Awwal.

questions.prompt: In which month did the Hijrah (migration) to Madinah take place?
questions.explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) arrived in Madinah in Rabi-ul-Awwal.

questions.prompt: Lailat-ul-Qadr falls in which month?
questions.explanation: Lailat-ul-Qadr is in the last ten nights of Ramadan.

questions.prompt: Which month is called the 'month of migration' (Shahr-ul-Hijrah)?
questions.explanation: The Hijri year begins with Muharram, the migration month.

questions.prompt: In which month did the Battle of Badr take place?
questions.explanation: Badr was fought in Ramadan, 2 AH.

questions.prompt: How many days are in an Islamic year?
questions.explanation: A lunar year is about 354 days.

questions.prompt: The month before Ramadan is:
questions.explanation: Sha'ban precedes Ramadan.

questions.prompt: In which month is Shab-e-Barat observed?
questions.explanation: Shab-e-Barat falls on 15 Sha'ban.

questions.prompt: Hajj is performed in which month?
questions.explanation: Hajj takes place in Dhul-Hijjah.

questions.prompt: Which month is known as the 'forbidden month' along with Rajab, Dhul-Qa'dah and Muharram?
questions.explanation: The four sacred months include Dhul-Hijjah.

questions.prompt: The Islamic year 1 AH corresponds to which Gregorian year?
questions.explanation: 1 AH began in 622 CE, the year of Hijrah.

questions.prompt: In which month is the Umrah at its peak during Ramadan?
questions.explanation: Umrah in Ramadan carries special reward.

questions.prompt: The '10th of Muharram' is known as:
questions.explanation: Ashura falls on 10 Muharram.

questions.prompt: Which month number is Rabi-ul-Awwal in the Islamic calendar?
questions.explanation: Rabi-ul-Awwal is the third month of the Hijri year.

questions.prompt: Which month follows Rabi-ul-Awwal?
questions.explanation: Rabi-ul-Akhir, the fourth month, comes after Rabi-ul-Awwal.

questions.prompt: Which month number is Jumada al-Ula?
questions.explanation: Jumada al-Ula is the fifth month of the Islamic calendar.

questions.prompt: Which month follows Jumada al-Ula?
questions.explanation: Jumada al-Akhirah, the sixth month, follows Jumada al-Ula.

questions.prompt: Which month number is Rajab?
questions.explanation: Rajab is the seventh month and one of the four sacred months.

questions.prompt: Which month comes immediately after Jumada al-Akhirah?
questions.explanation: Rajab, the seventh month, follows Jumada al-Akhirah.

questions.prompt: Which month number is Sha'ban?
questions.explanation: Sha'ban is the eighth month, directly before Ramadan.

questions.prompt: Which month number is Shawwal?
questions.explanation: Shawwal, the month of Eid-ul-Fitr, is the tenth month.

questions.prompt: Which month number is Dhul-Qa'dah?
questions.explanation: Dhul-Qa'dah is the eleventh month of the Islamic calendar.

questions.prompt: Which month precedes Dhul-Hijjah?
questions.explanation: Dhul-Qa'dah, the eleventh month, comes before Dhul-Hijjah.

questions.prompt: The Islamic weekday 'Al-Jumu'ah' corresponds to which day?
questions.explanation: Al-Jumu'ah is Friday, the day of congregational prayer.

questions.prompt: The Islamic weekday 'Al-Ahad' corresponds to which day?
questions.explanation: Al-Ahad is Sunday, the first day of the Islamic week.

questions.prompt: The Islamic weekday 'Al-Ithnayn' corresponds to which day?
questions.explanation: Al-Ithnayn is Monday, meaning 'the second day'.

questions.prompt: The Islamic weekday 'Ath-Thalatha' corresponds to which day?
questions.explanation: Ath-Thalatha is Tuesday — 'the third day'.

questions.prompt: The Islamic weekday 'Al-Arba'a' corresponds to which day?
questions.explanation: Al-Arba'a is Wednesday — 'the fourth day'.

questions.prompt: The Islamic weekday 'Al-Khamis' corresponds to which day?
questions.explanation: Al-Khamis is Thursday — 'the fifth day'.

questions.prompt: The Islamic weekday 'As-Sabt' corresponds to which day?
questions.explanation: As-Sabt is Saturday, the seventh day of the Islamic week.

questions.prompt: In Islamic tradition, when does the new day begin?
questions.explanation: The Islamic day begins at sunset, so nights precede their days.

questions.prompt: How many leap years does the Islamic calendar have in a 30-year cycle?
questions.explanation: The lunar calendar inserts eleven leap days over each 30-year cycle.

questions.prompt: How many days does each month of the Islamic calendar have?
questions.explanation: Lunar months are 29 or 30 days depending on the sighting of the moon.

questions.prompt: Which caliph introduced the official Islamic (Hijri) calendar?
questions.explanation: Umar (RA) established the Hijri calendar, dating from the Hijrah in 622 CE.

questions.prompt: In which month did the Prophet (PBUH) pass away?
questions.explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) passed away in Rabi-ul-Awwal, 11 AH.

questions.prompt: The 'white days' (Ayyam al-Bid) of each lunar month are which dates?
questions.explanation: Ayyam al-Bid are the 13th, 14th and 15th of each lunar month, when the moon is full.

questions.prompt: Fasting on the 'white days' of each month is?
questions.explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) recommended fasting the three white days each month.

questions.prompt: Which is the only sacred month that falls alone rather than consecutively?
questions.explanation: Rajab stands alone among the sacred months; the other three follow consecutively.

questions.prompt: The Quran describes Laylat-ul-Qadr as better than how many months?
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Qadr says the Night of Power is better than a thousand months.

questions.prompt: The Day of Arafah falls on which date?
questions.explanation: The Day of Arafah is the 9th of Dhul-Hijjah, the climax of Hajj.

questions.prompt: What is the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah called?
questions.explanation: The 8th of Dhul-Hijjah is Yawm at-Tarwiyah, when pilgrims set out for Mina.

questions.prompt: Zakat-ul-Fitr is paid before which prayer?
questions.explanation: Zakat-ul-Fitr is given before the Eid-ul-Fitr prayer so the poor may celebrate.

questions.prompt: The name 'Muharram' literally means?
questions.explanation: Muharram comes from the root haram — sacred, forbidden for fighting.

questions.prompt: The Islamic calendar takes its starting point (epoch) from which event?
questions.explanation: Year 1 AH begins with the Hijrah of the Prophet (PBUH) to Madinah in 622 CE.

questions.prompt: In which month was the Battle of Uhud fought?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Uhud took place in Shawwal, 3 AH.

questions.prompt: In which month was the Battle of the Trench (Khandaq) fought?
questions.explanation: The Battle of the Trench was fought in Shawwal, 5 AH.

questions.prompt: A leap year in the Islamic calendar has how many days?
questions.explanation: A leap Hijri year has 355 days; an ordinary one has 354.

questions.prompt: In the Islamic calendar, the extra day of a leap year is added to which month?
questions.explanation: The leap day is added to the last month, Dhul-Hijjah.

questions.prompt: Besides fasting, Ramadan is known as the month of what?
questions.explanation: Ramadan is called the month of mercy, forgiveness and the Quran.

questions.prompt: Laylat-ul-Qadr is most likely to be found among which nights?
options: The odd nights of the last ten of Ramadan
questions.explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) urged seeking Laylat-ul-Qadr in the odd nights of the final ten.

questions.prompt: The Islamic calendar is also known as the?
questions.explanation: The Islamic calendar is the Hijri lunar calendar.

questions.prompt: Which day of the week is described in hadith as the best day?
questions.explanation: Friday (Jumu'ah) is described as the best day, on which the sun rises.

questions.prompt: The two major Eids of Islam fall in which months?
questions.explanation: Eid-ul-Fitr is on 1 Shawwal and Eid-ul-Adha on 10 Dhul-Hijjah.

questions.prompt: What are the 11th, 12th and 13th of Dhul-Hijjah called?
questions.explanation: The 11th-13th of Dhul-Hijjah are Ayyam at-Tashriq, days of remembrance and takbir.

questions.prompt: The Hijri calendar is primarily used today for what purpose?
options: Determining religious observances such as Ramadan and Hajj
questions.explanation: Muslims use the Hijri calendar mainly to fix the times of worship and festivals.

questions.prompt: Which month comes right after Ramadan in the sequence of the Islamic year?
questions.explanation: Shawwal, the tenth month, immediately follows Ramadan.

questions.prompt: In which month do Muslims offer the six recommended fasts after Ramadan?
questions.explanation: Fasting six days of Shawwal is recommended, completing the reward of a full year.

questions.prompt: Which month is Safar in relation to Muharram?
questions.explanation: Safar is the second month, immediately after Muharram.

questions.prompt: How many months does the Islamic (lunar) year have?
questions.explanation: The Islamic year has twelve lunar months.

questions.prompt: Which is the fourth month of the Islamic calendar?
questions.explanation: Rabi-ul-Akhir is the fourth month of the Hijri year.

questions.prompt: Which month comes after Shawwal?
questions.explanation: Dhul-Qa'dah, the eleventh month, follows Shawwal.

questions.prompt: Apart from Ramadan, the Prophet (PBUH) fasted most in which month?
questions.explanation: Aisha (RA) said the Prophet (PBUH) fasted most in Sha'ban besides Ramadan.
